_comment: CF-A-NOTE-IS-NOT-A-RUNG. Rules for rewrite-parallel-names.cjs, first batch, from the 2026-09-26 spelling census (C:/tmp/spellcensus_2152/RESULT.md). Scope: baseball, 2024-2026, the same 15 Topps flagship + Bowman family setKeys the census paged across its 24 (setKey,year) pairs. SuperFractor is DELIBERATELY excluded (ruling pending -- sources disagree by year and 2 of 4 target sources were unreachable; see the census Step 4). Every rule below carries its own ruling, rulingDate and verbatim source quotes; a rule missing any of the three is refused by the lane at load, before any row is read.

rules.ruling: A retail/hobby/blaster/mega/super-box channel word glued onto the end of `parallel` is a checklistinsider-style page footnote about WHERE the card is sold, never part of the rung's own name -- clean rung is the text before the dash/colon.
sources: checklistinsider.com 2026 Topps Series 1: 'Purple Tinsel' and 'Yellow Tinsel' are the card names; '(Meijer exclusive)'/'(Walgreens exclusive)' is a separate parenthetical channel note on the same list line, using the site's uniform 'Name (channel exclusive)' convention for every parallel on the page -- not evidence the retailer text was meant to be part of the name.

Census Step 2 representative case: "Silver Crackle Foil - Super Box exclusive" (topps-update-series 2025 and siblings) -> name 'Silver Crackle Foil' (checklistinsider verbatim), no printRun stated on the one page reached.

rules.ruling: Same shape as strip-retailer-channel-word, on the Bowman family: a trailing channel word is a distribution footnote, never a rung name.
sources: checklistinsider.com 2026 Topps Series 1: 'Purple Tinsel' and 'Yellow Tinsel' are the card names; the retailer text is a separate parenthetical channel note on the same list line, the site's uniform convention -- generalised here to the sibling Bowman family pages using the identical list layout.

rules.ruling: A parenthetical naming a channel, an exclusivity claim, pack odds or a SKU is the same checklistinsider list-line convention documented for Purple/Yellow Tinsel -- a note ABOUT the card, appended on the source page, never the checklist's name for the rung.
sources: checklistinsider.com 2026 Topps Series 1: 'Purple Tinsel' / 'Yellow Tinsel' are the card names; '(Meijer exclusive)' / '(Walgreens exclusive)' is a separate parenthetical channel note on the same list line, using the site's uniform 'Name (channel exclusive)' convention for every parallel on the page.
Census Step 2: representative parenthetical-note shapes counted 28,772 rows corpus-wide across this family.

rules.ruling: Same parenthetical-channel-note shape, on the Bowman family.
sources: checklistinsider.com 2026 Topps Series 1: the uniform 'Name (channel exclusive)' list convention, generalised to the sibling Bowman family pages using the identical layout.

rules.ruling: "exclusive" appended after a dash (not inside parentheses) is the same channel-note convention as the parenthetical form, spelled without parens by a subset of source pages -- the clean rung is the text before the dash.
sources: checklistinsider.com 2026 Topps Series 1: retailer-exclusivity notes are consistently a footnote on the SAME line as the card's own name, never part of the name itself -- observed both parenthesized and dash-joined across the family's pages.
rules.reason: bare '- ... exclusive' suffix, not parenthesized (part of census's 71,852 'exclusive' rows)

rules.ruling: An inline print-run count glued onto `parallel` (e.g. 'Crackle Foil: 10,400 copies') states the SAME number `printRun` exists to carry -- moved there, never left in the name, and only when a checklist-grade row elsewhere in the same product already attests that exact rung+run (this lane refuses to mint an unconfirmed run on its own say-so).
sources: Census Step 2 representative case: "Crackle Foil: 10,400 copies" (topps 2026) -> name 'Crackle Foil', printRun: 10400 -- checklist (checklistinsider convention elsewhere on this family) states a numeric run for this rung.
rules.reason: inline print-run count (census: 97,610 rows). Explicitly excludes the topps 2024 Aqua Series One/Series Two cross-series breakdown strings (4,144 rows) and the topps-update-series 2024 Platinum run-on-digit corruption (~3,334 rows) -- both flagged for Drew in the census, not auto-fixable by a text-strip rule.

rules.ruling: Same inline print-run-count shape, on the Bowman family.
sources: Census Step 2: the inline print-run pattern is corpus-wide across the Topps/Bowman flagship family (97,610 rows total); the Crackle Foil example generalises directly.

rules.ruling: A per-pack/per-box odds statement ('8 per Celebration Box', '1:24') is a distribution fact about the PRODUCT, not the rung's name -- checklistinsider's own Confetti / Confetti - 8 per Celebration Box pair is exactly this shape.
sources: Census Step 1 table: topps 2025 'Confetti / Confetti - 8 per Celebration Box.' (697 / 1865 rows) -> LEAKED NOTE, not a spelling split -- clean rung 'Confetti'.
rules.reason: per-pack/per-box odds count + 1:N pack odds (census: 12,097 + 752 rows)

rules.ruling: A trailing SKU/item code is a retailer catalog number, never part of the checklist's own name for the rung.
sources: Census Step 2 pattern table: SKU-suffixed rows counted 4,992 corpus-wide, the same trailing-annotation shape as the channel-word and odds patterns above, differing only in what follows the dash.

rules.ruling: Two independent sources agree verbatim on the closed-compound, cap-R-cap-W spelling for every color; sale-title language overwhelmingly favors it (38:1). 'Raywave Refractor' (beckett-sourced, ~300-466 rows/color) is the minority misspelling and folds onto the majority row.
sources: checklistinsider.com 2025: 'RayWave Refractor' (cap R, cap W) verbatim, every color.
Census title-phrase evidence: "raywave" in 3,283 vs "ray wave" in 86 of 50,001 sampled 2025 Topps Chrome sold_comps titles.
rules.reason: RayWave Refractor spelling fold, all 6 colors (census: ~18,300 rows across the cluster)

rules.ruling: Apostrophe-dropping is a checklistinsider ingestion habit seen repeatedly across this family (Father's/Fathers Day, Mother's/Mother's Day elsewhere); the proper-noun possessive form is restored.
sources: Census Step 1 table: topps-series-2 2024 'Mother's Day Hot Pink / Mothers Day Hot Pink' (460 / 1797 rows) -> FOLD -> 'Mother's Day Hot Pink' (apostrophe present) -- apostrophe-dropping is a checklistinsider ingestion habit seen elsewhere (Father's/Fathers Day, Mother's/Mother's below).
rules.reason: apostrophe restore, Mother's Day Hot Pink

rules.ruling: Same apostrophe-dropping pattern as the Mother's Day pair in the same product/year.
sources: Census Step 1 table: topps-series-2 2024 'Father's Day Powder Blue / Fathers Day Powder Blue' (416 / 1797 rows) -> FOLD -> 'Father's Day Powder Blue'.
rules.reason: apostrophe restore, Father's Day Powder Blue

rules.ruling: Pure encoding variant -- curly apostrophe (U+2019) vs ASCII ' -- folded to the ASCII form the catalog stores as canonical.
sources: Census Step 1 table: topps-update-series 2024 'Mother's Day Hot Pink / Mother’s Day Hot Pink (curly apostrophe)' (438 / 916 rows) -> FOLD -> straight ' (ASCII) as the stored canonical, cosmetic-only.

rules.ruling: Proper-noun capitalization of 'Lantern' restored; the majority-cased form is also the grammatically correct one.
sources: Census Step 1 table: topps-update-series 2024 'Jack O'lantern / Jack O'Lantern' (427 / 350 rows) -> FOLD -> 'Jack O'Lantern' (proper-noun capitalization).

rules.ruling: Majority spelling plus internal consistency with the Fractor-family capitalization convention already established by SuperFractor/RayWave (cap the second element).
sources: Census Step 1 table: bowman-chrome 2026 'Bowman Logofractor / Bowman LogoFractor' (8 / 739 rows) -> FOLD -> 'Bowman LogoFractor' (majority + matches Fractor-family capitalization convention seen in SuperFractor/RayWave).
